 Wedgewood pharmacy voluntarily recalls compounded veterinary medications due to potency concerns
 Wedgewood Pharmacy is recalling several compounded veterinary medications that were shipped to pet owners, veterinary practices, and pharmacies over the last several months. The company is working to alert affected customers, provide refunds or replacements, and suggest clinical alternatives where appropriate.
 Emily Singler, VMD 
 Published Oct 23, 2026 
 Share

 email 
 Advertisement
 Wedgewood Pharmacy announced a voluntary recall of certain veterinary compounded medications intended for use in companion, equine, exotic, zoo, wildlife, and aquatic species. This recall was initiated due to “inconsistencies in the reliability of certain analytical testing data generated by their laboratory,” according to an announcement issued by the company on October 21, 2026.
 These inconsistencies may have resulted in the production of subpotent and/or superpotent products, the announcement explained, noting that the company detected the inconsistencies through their own quality control processes. “Quality is our top priority at Wedgewood,” said Rae Hutchins, DVM, DACVIM, Chief Veterinary Officer of Wedgewood Pharmacy. “When we identified concerns about the reliability of certain laboratory testing data, we determined that voluntarily recalling affected medications was the responsible course of action.”
 The affected products
 The affected medications were shipped throughout the U.S. between February 18, 2026, and October 6, 2026, to veterinary practices, pharmacies, and pet owners. A full list of affected products, which include powders, pastes, oral suspensions, injectables, ophthalmic ointments and solutions, ear solutions and suspensions, topical sprays, and gels, can be found here .
 The company reports having received 98 complaints thus far, 7 of which they classified as serious. According to Hutchins, the complaints represent approximately 0.04% of prescriptions affected by the recall. Nonetheless, she said, “we take every report seriously and continue to carefully evaluate the information available.”
 Recall action steps
 “As a veterinarian, I understand the concern this voluntary recall has created for veterinary teams and the families whose animals depend on these medications,” Hutchins said. “We’re committed to supporting our veterinary colleagues and the animals in their care throughout this process.”
 Wedgewood said in their announcement that they are working to notify affected customers and arrange for a refund or a replacement of recalled products where possible. “Our veterinary and customer support teams are working closely with practices to answer questions and identify clinically appropriate alternatives where available,” Hutchins added.
 Customers who have an affected product should stop using it and contact Wedgewood’s recall services at 866-562-5931, Monday through Friday, 8AM to 9 PM ET and Saturday 9AM to 5PM ET.
 Any suspected adverse reactions or quality concerns associated with an affected product should be reported to the FDA at 1-888-FDA-VETS or at www.FDA.gov/reportanimalae .
